messages:
Maya: quick follow-up on the onboarding pipeline RFC — we need to decide the split of responsibilities: lightweight runtime smoke vs heavy offline bench. do we gate admission on full bench results or allow a fast-path with runtime feature flags?
Sergio: +1 to clarifying tradeoffs. my worry: full bench pre-admit blocks velocity for new models, but letting too much to runtime increases outage blast radius.
Anika: i sketched a middle path in the doc — two-tier admit: quick heuristics (format, shape, basic ops) then admit to a staging pool that runs the full bench async and can auto-suggest rollback.
Devon: can we make the staging pool traffic-weighted so prod traffic only hits it for a small % during initial rollout? that reduces risk.
Ravi: technically fine, but we need a clean contract between intake and runtime. current ingest <-> runtime handshake is ad-hoc (some proto fields, env flags). i'd like a minimal, versioned handshake.
Maya: agreed. propose a small JSON handshake with fields: model_id, fingerprint, runtime_compat, bench_state. if bench_state==pending the router applies canary routing. thoughts?
Sergio: sounds good. example payload?
Anika: posted a sample in the RFC but here's a compact one we can use in the wire:```{
  "model_id": "m4-llama-13b-q4",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:abcd1234",
  "onnx_ok": true,
  "kv_schema_v": "2",
  "bench_state": "pending"
}```
Devon: +1 to versioned fields. what about model variants (quantized vs fp16)? need to include variant_id or runtime_profile.
Ravi: add "variant": "q4_0" and a small capabilities map like ["kv_cache","n_head_shard"]. keep it small so edge services can do fast checks.
Maya: operational flow I'm imagining: 1) ingest runs linter & basic smoke 2) if pass, model goes to staging with bench_state=pending 3) bench fleet consumes and sets bench_state=passed/failed 4) router enforces canary policies while pending.
Sergio: call out timeouts. bench should have SLAs (e.g., 24h to finish) else mark stale and fall back to conservative routing. also need manual override.
Anika: agree. also surface bench metadata in Console: token perf, p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, regressions vs golden set. that helps product teams.
Devon: on the runtime side we need a compact liveness probe for model binaries: small inference smoke that validates KV cache correctness + typical seq length. cheap and fast (<200ms). if that fails runtime should circuit-break.
Ravi: we can reuse existing kv-healthcheck but standardize inputs. propose a small stash of golden prompts as part of model artifact. bench will validate full evals, runtime uses 3 quick probes.
InfraBot: bench-pool-alpha created: 12 workers, q4 optimized. enqueue API: POST /bench/enqueue {model_id} — ETA 2-6h per model.
Maya: thanks infra. 2 followups: (a) policy for partial bench results (some tests pass, some fail) — default to failed unless policy allows specific ignored checks, (b) migration plan for existing models that lack fingerprinting.
Sergio: (a) sounds safe. we can allow per-team policy overrides via Console (opt-ins). (b) for legacy models we create a retro fingerprint job and backfill bench_state=passed if it completes. keep legacy models in a legacy_mode flag until backfilled.
Anika: note: we should avoid reinventing feature flags. use routing-layer rules: route by bench_state + team opt-in + traffic percentage. keep router evaluation fast (in-memory map).
Devon: implementation note: the ingest->registry->router chain should rely on a compact k/v store (etcd or Redis) for quick lookups. registry writes should be atomic and versioned.
Ravi: agree on atomic writes. also include a monotonic config version to allow rollbacks if bench metadata is wrong.
Maya: ok actions: @Sergio + @Anika to write a small adaptor RFC for the handshake JSON + router semantics; @InfraBot to expand bench-pool capacity doc; @Devon to draft runtime smoke probe definition; @Ravi to propose registry write schema. target: next week sync. :thumbsup:
Sergio: I'm on it.
Anika: will draft and link the example tests.
Devon: drafting probe now.
Ravi: will spec the schema and backfill plan.
InfraBot: bench-pool-alpha scaling doc: https://internal.redwood/bench/alpha-scaling — added notes on region affinity and cost estimates.
Maya: perfect. thanks team — if no blockers i'll merge the small followup RFC by EOD and we can start the staging rollouts. :rocket:
